tier: isolated local SQL/filesystem fixtures and loopback HTTPS

resource_api.retry_policy: no-replace link; retry only Windows sharing error 32/33, four attempts, total delay at most 500ms
resource_api.persistent_sharing_lock: retryable resource_io_unknown; stage and journal preserved for authenticated same-request recovery
resource_api.private_directive: P2 read_step_directive/current workspace scope grant + current run/session/version + owner/source-bound F5 context; explicit F9 child grant required
resource_api.session_environment: registered nonempty session and environment required for publish/read/recover

coverage: hash-bound publish/read, replay, tamper detection and same-scope content deduplication
scope/device/session authorization, missing session/environment rejection and private-purpose downgrade protection
actual P2/F5 current-owner directive read and F9 child scope-binding read
stale context, removed scope lock, wrong owner and stale directive version rejection
bounded WinError 32 retry, persistent sharing lock recovery with same request, and no retry for other file errors
staged and published-file recovery across a simulated DB commit interruption

loopback_https_tests.observed: 8 MiB bounded upload/readback, hash check, cross-scope denial, oversize rejection and wrong-CA rejection
graph snapshot upload/readback, Host source pointer, F2 rebuild/query, F5 bounded response validation and local-only rejection
two authenticated clients, request replay and claim race, scope filtering and device revocation on cached requests

limitations: Loopback HTTPS fixtures use a generated local certificate and isolated temporary databases.
No external reverse proxy, deployed Host, Linux Host or production installation was tested.

The separate Windows fixture sharing-lock and readonly-database errors remain documented in windows-fixture-errors.json; targeted runs after the fixes passed, but the failures are retained as historical fixture observations.
